title: rorca-browser-mcp-integration
specName: Browser MCP Integration — Playwright HTTP server injected into all three agent types
description: Adds first-class browser testing capability to Rorca execution engine for all three agent types (claude, opencode, codex). A spec or story sets `browserMcp: true` — execution-engine detects this flag (100% explicit, no heuristics), starts a @playwright/mcp HTTP server on port 4040 (idempotent singleton per engine process), then injects it via the agent's native config mechanism: `--mcp-config` for claude, a per-story `opencode.json` written to cwd for opencode, and `codex mcp add/remove` lifecycle for codex. Zero user setup required. Graceful fallback if @playwright/mcp fails to start.

userStories.title: Story loop integration — resolve browserMcp per story, start server, inject URL, enrich prompt and WAL event
userStories.description:
Wire everything together inside the `executeStory()` function in `backend/src/lib/execution-engine.ts`.

`executeStory()` is the function starting around line 2224. It receives `story: UserStory` and `config: EngineConfig` but does NOT currently receive the full `SpecJson`. The `storyWantsBrowserMcp()` helper needs the spec object, so we add it as a new optional final parameter.

## Step 1: Add `spec` parameter to executeStory()

Add `spec?: SpecJson` as the new final optional parameter after `waveIndex?: number`:

```typescript
async function executeStory(
  story: UserStory,
  config: EngineConfig,
  mode: 'impl' | 'qa',
  playbook: string | undefined,
  logDir: string,
  workspaceId: string | null,
  retryCounts: Map<string, number>,
  storyCwd?: string,
  worktreeInfo?: StoryWorktree,
  _escalationStatesRemoved?: unknown,
  allStories?: UserStory[],
  storyAgentOverride?: AgentType,
  storyAttachAddr?: string | null,
  personaRegistry?: PersonaRegistry,
  waveIndex?: number,
  spec?: SpecJson,
): Promise<'passed' | 'failed' | 'skipped'>
```

## Step 2: Update the sequential call site in main()

In the sequential loop (`main()`), `currentSpec` is already read at the top of each iteration (around line 3132): `const currentSpec: SpecJson = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(config.jsonPath, 'utf8'))`. Pass it as the final argument:

```typescript
const seqResult = await executeStory(
  story, config, mode, playbook, logDir, workspaceId, retryCounts,
  undefined, undefined, undefined, currentStories,
  undefined, undefined, personaRegistry,
  undefined, // waveIndex
  currentSpec, // spec — for storyWantsBrowserMcp()
);
```

## Step 3: Update the parallel call site in runParallel()

Find where `executeStory()` is called inside `runParallel()`. Read the spec JSON once before the wave loop and pass it:

```typescript
// Read spec once for browserMcp resolution (at the start of runParallel, before wave loop)
const specForBrowserMcp: SpecJson = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(config.jsonPath, 'utf8'));
```

Then in each `executeStory()` call within runParallel, add `specForBrowserMcp` as the final argument.

## Step 4: Inside executeStory(), add browser MCP logic before buildPrompt()

Find the section between the `story_started` WAL event emission (around line 2402) and the `buildPrompt()` call. Insert:

```typescript
// Resolve browser MCP for this story
const wantsBrowser = storyWantsBrowserMcp(story, spec ?? {});
let browserMcpUrl: string | null = null;
if (wantsBrowser) {
  browserMcpUrl = await ensurePlaywrightMcpServer();
  if (browserMcpUrl) {
    process.stdout.write(`[BrowserMCP] Browser tools active for story ${story.id}\n`);
  }
}
```

## Step 5: Add `browser_mcp` to story_started WAL event

The story_started WAL event is emitted around line 2404. Add `browser_mcp: wantsBrowser` to its payload object:

```typescript
await emitWalEvent(config.port, 'story_started', workspaceId, {
  run_id: config.runId,
  story_id: story.id,
  story_title: story.title,
  agent_type: effectiveAgent,
  log_file: storyLogFile,
  browser_mcp: wantsBrowser,
  // ... all existing spread fields unchanged ...
}, story.id);
```

## Step 6: Enrich prompt when wantsBrowser is true

The `prompt` variable is built by `buildPrompt()`. After `buildPrompt()` returns the prompt string and before the `while(true)` rate-limit retry loop, append the browser section:

```typescript
if (wantsBrowser && browserMcpUrl) {
  prompt += [
    '',
    '## Browser MCP',
    'The `playwright` MCP server is active for this story. Use it for all UI verification:',
    '- `browser_navigate` — navigate to a URL',
    '- `browser_snapshot` — capture accessibility snapshot of current page',
    '- `browser_click` / `browser_type` — interact with elements',
    '- `browser_console_messages` — read JS console output',
    '- `browser_network_requests` — inspect network activity',
    '',
    'Do NOT fall back to headless Chrome CLI (`/Applications/Google Chrome.app/...`). Use the playwright MCP tools exclusively.',
  ].join('\n');
}
```

## Step 7: Pass browserMcpUrl to runAgent()

The `runAgent()` call is inside the `while(true)` rate-limit retry loop (around line 2458). Add `browserMcpUrl` as the final argument:

```typescript
const result = await runAgent(
  effectiveAgent,
  prompt,
  effectiveCwd,
  timeoutMin * 60 * 1000,
  storyLogFile,
  currentModel,
  effectiveAttach,
  tokenUpdateCallback,
  config.thinkingEnabled,
  config.thinkingBudget,
  config.effortLevel,
  browserMcpUrl,
);
```

Note: `browserMcpUrl` is declared before the while loop so it is in scope inside the loop.
